h1: Your Google Business Profile, fixed and defended
metaTitle: Google Business Profile Optimisation and Reinstatement
metaDescription: Google Business Profile optimisation including suspension and reinstatement work — the failure that quietly stops Indian service businesses from ranking.
answer: Google Business Profile optimisation means getting your categories, services, attributes, photos and posts right, then defending them. In India the bigger job is usually suspension: coworking addresses, home-based service businesses and keyword-stuffed names get listings pulled, and reinstatement is a documented appeal with evidence, not a support ticket. From ₹40,000 a month.
takeaways: **Primary category is the single biggest lever** on the profile. Most Indian listings have the wrong one and have never changed it.
Suspension is the failure mode nobody sells against. Coworking addresses, home-based service businesses and name-stuffing account for most of it.
Anyone can edit your listing. Competitors do. We snapshot your profile weekly and revert what changed.
Geotagging your photos does nothing — Google strips the metadata on upload. It's the most persistently sold non-service in Indian local SEO.
Export your profile performance data on day one. Google only shows six months, and a baseline you didn't save is a baseline you can't prove.

sections.h2: The build-out, in the order that actually matters
body: A Google Business Profile has about thirty fields and roughly four of them decide whether you appear in the map pack. Filling all thirty in the wrong order is how agencies produce a 100%-complete profile that still doesn't rank.
numbered: **Primary category.** This is the lever. Google matches queries to categories before it looks at anything you wrote. We check what the businesses already ranking in your pack use, and pick accordingly — a clinic listed as 'Doctor' instead of 'Dermatologist' is competing in the wrong race entirely.
**Secondary categories, sparingly.** Each one you add makes you eligible for more queries and slightly less specific for your main one. Five relevant beats fifteen hopeful.
**Services, with descriptions.** Every service you sell, named the way customers say it, with a written description under each. This is free text Google reads and most profiles leave it blank.

**Photos, on a schedule.** Exterior with signage, interior, team, work in progress, products. Fresh uploads monthly. Geotagging them changes nothing — Google strips EXIF data on upload — and any vendor charging for it is charging for a myth.
**Posts, weekly.** Offers, updates and events. They expire, which is the point: an actively posted profile signals an actively operating business.
**Q&A, seeded honestly.** You're allowed to ask and answer questions on your own profile. Do it with the five questions your front desk answers daily.
**Hours, including holiday hours.** A profile showing 'Open' when the shutter is down generates a one-star review that costs more than a year of posts.

callout.title: Distance is a factor you cannot optimise
callout.body: Google's local ranking has three inputs: relevance, distance and prominence. You can work on two of them. Nobody can make a Whitefield clinic outrank an Indiranagar clinic for someone standing in Indiranagar, and any agency promising map-pack position one is quietly hoping you never search from a different postcode.

sections.h2: Why Indian listings get suspended, and what the appeal actually involves
body: This is the part of local SEO nobody puts on a services page, because it's messy and the outcome isn't in the agency's control. It's also the reason a large share of Indian service businesses have no local visibility at all.
A suspension arrives with no warning and no specific explanation. The listing simply disappears from Maps and Search, and the dashboard shows a generic notice.

table.caption: The most common suspension triggers we see on Indian profiles.
head: What triggers it
Why Google flags it
What fixes it
rows: Coworking or virtual office address
Multiple unrelated businesses at one verified address
A signed desk with your own signage, or convert to a service-area business and hide the address
Keyword-stuffed business name
"Best Dental Clinic in Andheri | Dr Sharma" isn't the name on your board
Revert to the legal or signage name before appealing. Nothing else works while it's stuffed

Hide the address, define service areas, keep the address on file for verification

Change one field at a time, then wait. Never batch NAP edits
Multiple listings at the same address
Duplicate or lead-generation listings
Remove or merge the duplicates yourself before appealing, and say you've done it

body: Six steps, in this order. The order is the part people get wrong.
bullets: **Stop editing.** Every further change while suspended weakens the appeal. First rule, most commonly broken.
**Diagnose the actual cause** by comparing the profile against the guideline it most likely violated, then fix that first. Appealing without fixing wastes a clean attempt.

**Assemble the evidence pack.** Photo of external signage with the business name visible, utility bill or registered rent agreement, GST certificate, incorporation or Udyam registration, and a bank statement header. Real documents in the business's real name.
**File the reinstatement request** through the Business Profile support flow, with a short factual account of what changed and what's been corrected. No pleading, no keywords.

**Prepare for video verification.** Google often asks for a single unbroken recording: street, signage, entrance, the working space, tools or stock, and something proving you control the premises. We script and rehearse it — a re-shoot costs you another week.
**One appeal per rejection, with new evidence.** Resubmitting the identical case gets auto-closed.

callout.title: We can't guarantee reinstatement, and neither can anyone else
callout.body: The decision sits with Google's review team and there's no route beyond the published appeal process. What we commit to is a correctly diagnosed cause, a complete evidence pack and a properly filed appeal — plus telling you early if the listing is genuinely ineligible, so you stop paying for a fight you cannot win.

sections.h2: Service-area businesses: the rules when there's no walk-in
body: Plumbers, electricians, packers and movers, home tutors, mobile diagnostics, cloud kitchens without a counter — most of India's service economy falls here, and most of it is configured wrongly.

A service-area business hides its street address and declares the areas it serves, up to twenty. Google still places your pin at your verified address, and distance still applies from there. Listing all of Mumbai does not make you appear across all of Mumbai. That's the honest limit, and it changes what's worth spending on: for a business serving three suburbs from one base, the [website's local pages](/compare/google-business-profile-vs-website) will carry the queries the profile can't reach.
bullets: Hide the address if customers don't come to you. A visible residential address is a standing suspension risk.
Service areas should be somewhere you'd genuinely travel to — a two-hour drive is a sensible ceiling.
One profile per genuine location. A second listing for a second suburb you don't operate from is a duplicate, and it will eventually take the original down with it.
Keep the verification documents current. When Google re-verifies — and it does, without notice — you have days, not weeks.

sections.h2: Weekly defence, because anyone can edit your listing
body: Your Google Business Profile is the only marketing asset you own that strangers can edit. The 'Suggest an edit' button is open to any signed-in user, and Google applies plausible-looking edits without asking you.

In competitive Indian categories — dentists, coaching institutes, gyms, packers and movers, real estate — this gets used deliberately. Hours changed to closed. Category swapped. Website URL replaced. A rival files a spam report against your name.
bullets: **Weekly snapshot and diff.** We store the full profile and compare it every week: name, categories, hours, phone, website, attributes, address. Anything that changed without your say-so gets reverted the same week.
**Duplicate hunting.** Aggregators and old directory feeds spawn duplicate listings that split your reviews and confuse Google. We find them and get them merged or removed.

**Spam reporting, both directions.** Competitors stuffing keywords into their business names get reported through the Redressal Complaint Form, with evidence. It works more often than founders expect, and it's free.
**Review monitoring** with response turnaround inside 48 hours. Review work at scale sits in [review management](/services/review-management-services), which pairs with this one.

sections.h2: Price, and the baseline the guarantee runs on
body: Profile management starts at **₹40,000 a month**, ex-GST, month-to-month after the first quarter with 30 days' notice. Multi-location businesses are quoted per location with a sharp drop after the fifth. Suspension recovery is included for clients on retainer; as a standalone piece of work it's quoted case by case, because a name-stuffing fix and a coworking-address fight are not the same job.

Our company guarantee runs on qualified leads from organic search, frozen for the trailing 90 days on day one. On a profile engagement we freeze two more numbers from your Business Profile performance report: **calls** and **direction requests**. If we haven't beaten your frozen baseline in 90 days, we keep working free until we do.

One practical warning that costs people their proof: Google's performance data only reaches back six months in the interface. We export and store yours in week one. If your last agency didn't, the baseline they claim to have improved on doesn't exist anymore.

What we will never quote is a map-pack position. Two people standing on the same street can see different packs, because distance is weighted per searcher. A ranking guarantee on a local pack is either ignorance or a sales tactic, and both are expensive. Full pricing sits on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faqs.q: How much does Google Business Profile management cost in India?
faqs.a: Freelancers charge ₹5,000–₹15,000 a month for posting and basic edits. Agencies doing real work — category strategy, weekly defence, citation cleanup, suspension handling — charge ₹25,000–₹75,000 a month per location. Ours starts at ₹40,000 a month ex-GST, with per-location pricing that drops after five.

faqs.q: Why was my Google Business Profile suspended?
faqs.a: Most Indian suspensions come down to five causes: a coworking or virtual address, a keyword-stuffed business name, a home address shown publicly for a service business, rapid edits to name or address after verification, or duplicate listings at one address. Google doesn't tell you which. Diagnosing it correctly is most of the work.

Anywhere from a few days to several weeks, and it depends on the cause, the quality of your evidence and whether video verification is requested. Nobody can promise an outcome or a date. What we can promise is a correctly diagnosed cause and a complete appeal, filed once and properly.

faqs.q: Does posting on Google Business Profile help rankings?
faqs.a: Posts aren't a strong direct ranking factor, but they keep the profile active, occupy space in your listing and give searchers a reason to click. The heavier levers are your primary category, review volume and velocity, proximity to the searcher, and citation consistency. Post weekly, but don't expect posts alone to move the pack.

faqs.q: Do geotagged photos improve local rankings?
faqs.a: No. Google strips EXIF metadata from images on upload, so the geotag never survives to be read. It remains one of the most confidently sold non-services in Indian local SEO. Upload real, current photos regularly — the freshness and the subject matter matter, the invisible coordinates don't.

faqs.q: Can I rank in a city where I don't have an address?
faqs.a: In the map pack, barely — proximity is weighted from your verified pin, and service areas expand eligibility rather than reach. Renting a fake address is a suspension waiting to happen. The realistic route is location pages on your own website plus links and citations from that city.
